title: Incomplete Bicliques for Block-Cipher Cryptanalysis
summary: Standard biclique cryptanalysis uses complete bipartite graphs; whether incomplete graphs enable new tradeoffs in success, complexity, and round coverage remains open.

formal_statement.body: In biclique cryptanalysis of block ciphers, investigate constructions that replace a complete biclique—a complete bipartite graph—with a more general, incomplete graph, and determine whether such constructions yield new tradeoffs among attack success probability, complexity requirements, and the number of cipher rounds attacked.

scope.domain: Biclique cryptanalysis of block ciphers using generalized, incomplete graph structures.
parameters: Attack success probability: a tradeoff criterion
Complexity requirements: a resource tradeoff criterion
Number of cipher rounds attacked: the round-coverage criterion
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether generalized incomplete-graph constructions yield new tradeoffs among attack success probability, complexity requirements, and the number of attacked rounds.

citations.label: Biclique Cryptanalysis of the Full AES

progress.summary: The source proposes dropping the completeness requirement on bicliques and considering more general graphs. It presents possible new tradeoffs in success probability, complexity, and round coverage as an open direction.
citation_labels: Andrey Bogdanov et al., Biclique Cryptanalysis of the Full AES
